title: [YouPass Collect] - Overseas student residence patterns in Australia: 1982-2000
prompt: The graph below shows four countries of residence of overseas students in Australia. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the number of international students from four Asian countries who came to Australia for educational purposes between 1982 and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all four countries experienced an upward trend in student numbers throughout the given period, despite some fluctuations. Additionally, Malaysia started with the highest figure, but was eventually surpassed by Indonesia, which recorded the highest number by 2000.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at countries with sharper increases and subsequent declines, Indonesia began at zero in 1982 and rose gradually to 10,000 students by 1994. From there, the figure surged dramatically to peak at roughly 26,000 in 1998, before falling back to around 23,000 by 2000. Similarly, Hong Kong started later, with around 5,000 students in 1988, then climbed steadily to approximately 19,000 in 1997. However, this was followed by a decline to 14,000 in 1999, though the number recovered slightly to 18,000 in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding countries with more consistent growth patterns, Singapore started from zero while Malaysia recorded the highest initial figure of close to 5,000 in 1982. Singapore experienced steady growth throughout, multiplying nearly twentyfold to reach just under 20,000 by 2000, thereby overtaking Malaysia as the second most popular destination. Meanwhile, Malaysia more than tripled to peak at approximately 17,500 in 1997, then declined to around 15,000 in 1999, before recovering to roughly 17,000 in the final year, remaining in third place.
